title: FreeIPA Flaw Chain Lets Anonymous Clients Create Reusable Administrator Credentials
blurb: A chained set of FreeIPA flaws lets an unauthenticated client mint reusable admin credentials -- a serious blow to identity infrastructure relying on FreeIPA for directory trust.

title: Telerik UI Padding-Oracle Bug Chained to Unauthenticated RCE — Public Exploit Released
blurb: A padding-oracle flaw in Telerik UI chains to unauthenticated remote code execution, and a public exploit is now circulating -- patch immediately if you run affected apps.

title: ClearFake WebDAV infection chain delivers Amatera stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
blurb: **Problem:** Cisco Talos traced a malware chain after spotting a DLL named "verification.google" launching from a WebDAV path at a Ukrainian government org. **Approach, in plain words:** Victims on a compromised site see a fake Google CAPTCHA ("ClickFix") tricking them into pasting and running a command. That opens a WebDAV path and runs a disguised DLL via `rundll32.exe`. The overlay JavaScript comes from BNB Smart Chain contracts (EtherHiding), letting the attacker update payloads without hosting them. **Result:** The chains deliver Amatera plus either a Zig-based crypto stealer with an EDR-killing driver, or a rogue NetSupport remote-access tool with Russian C2. **Why it matters:** Shows how attackers blend social engineering, legitimate protocols, and blockchain hosting for stealthy, takedown-resistant delivery. **Glossary:** WebDAV (protocol letting Windows mount and run files from a remote server like a local drive); ClickFix (social engineering that tricks a user into manually running a malicious command); EtherHiding (storing/serving malicious code via blockchain smart contracts instead of a normal web server); C2 (command-and-control, the attacker's server issuing instructions to installed malware).

title: New DLSS 5 mod offloads Neural Rendering to a second card massively cutting the AI filter's performance hit
blurb: A community mod splits DLSS 5's neural rendering workload onto a dedicated second GPU, recovering much of the frame-rate DLSS 5 otherwise costs.

title: As the western games industry struggles, China's games industry is booming, a new report shows
blurb: A new market report puts China's games industry at roughly $50 billion, growing sharply while western studios face layoffs and cutbacks.

title: AI Has Solved One of Math's $1 Million Millennium Prize Problems
blurb: **Problem:** Do the Navier-Stokes equations, describing fluid flow, ever "blow up" to infinite speed at a point? One of six unsolved Millennium Prize Problems. **Approach, in plain words:** Two efforts converged. OpenAI ran 10,000 AI agents attacking it directly. Separately, mathematicians Buckmaster and Alpöge extended prior techniques, stacking "infinite layers" of well-behaved solutions into cascades that force a blow-up. **Result:** A proof that singularities exist in the boundary-free 3D case, formally checked by the Lean proof assistant -- the biggest AI-assisted math proof yet. **Why it matters:** AI cracked a previously intractable open problem, and turbulence is confirmed stranger than assumed: flow can turn infinitely violent at a point. **Glossary:** Navier-Stokes equations (the standard equations for how fluids like water and air move, accounting for viscosity); singularity/blow-up (a point where a quantity, here fluid speed, becomes infinite); Euler equations (the frictionless simplification of Navier-Stokes); Lean (a programming language/proof assistant that mechanically checks a proof's logic).

title: Some black holes grow much faster than their galaxies
blurb: New observations find supermassive black holes outpacing the growth of their host galaxies, challenging assumptions about how the two evolve together.

title: I've factored the RSA keys of a Certificate Authority…from the 90s
blurb: A researcher factored weak RSA keys from a 1990s Certificate Authority, a hands-on look at just how breakable early web-PKI cryptography really was.

title: Reverse engineering my e-scooter and rewriting the firmware in rust
blurb: A documented teardown of an e-scooter's electronics and protocol, culminating in a full firmware rewrite in Rust.

title: Kimi K3 (2.8T) at 1 token/s on a MacBook Pro, streamed from four SSDs
blurb: A build log for running a 2.8-trillion-parameter model on consumer hardware by streaming weights off four SSDs instead of holding them in RAM.
